Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Cyient Limited’s Q2 FY2027 results 
conference call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there 
will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Please note 
that this call is being recorded. I now hand over the conference to Mr. Krishna Bodanapu, 
Executive Vice Chairman and Managing Director. Thank you and over to you, Sir. 
Krishna Bodanapu: 
Thank you very much and good evening ladies and gentlemen. Welcome to Cyient 
Limited’s earnings call for Q2 of FY2027. I am Krishna Bodanapu, Executive Vice-
Chairman & Managing Director, and present with me on this call are Sukamal Banerjee, 
Executive Director & CEO, and Shrinivas Kulkarni, Chief Financial Officer. I would like to 
mention that some of the statements made in today’s discussions may be forward-looking in 
nature and may involve risks and uncertainties. A detailed statement in this regard is 
available in our investor update and has been e-mailed to you and is also posted on our 
corporate website. This call will be accompanied by an earnings call presentation, the 
details of which have already been shared with you. We are reporting group performance 
under four segments DET, DLM, Semiconductors and others. The focus of this call, as 
always, will remain the DET segment, and the group numbers will include performance of 
all four segments. I will start with a brief update of our Semiconductor business and our 
DLM business before Sukamal and Shrini walk you through DET’s performance. 
 
Firstly, I would like to take a minute to give you a bit of background on the Semiconductor 
business and how we work there. Cyient Semiconductors operates through two businesses 
the first is our custom ASIC business where we take a customer’s requirement for a chip 
from specification to silicon and then supply it in production in volumes. These programs 
give us long-term customer relationships and the designs that carry into volume supply, 
which means that there is an annuity-based revenue stream. The second and very important 
for our long-term strategy is our product or ASSP strategy in business. Here we develop our 
own chips and sell them to multiple customers so the IP is fully owned and reusable by 
Cyient. This includes the low voltage portfolio that we acquired through the acquisition of 
Kinetic Technologies and on the high voltage products we are now developing. 
Applications include AI, data centers, industrial and automotive. 
 
The quarterly performance for the business was very strong. Revenue for the quarter was 
$19.3 million, which was up 8% quarter-on-quarter. This is our sixth consecutive quarter of 
sequential growth, a record we are proud of, and one that reflects the breadth of our 
portfolio. Order momentum remains healthy, and order intake on our custom ASIC business 
is up more than 50% compared to last quarter. EBIT margin improved against previous 
quarter even as we kept funding R&D, talent and go-to-market much ahead of the revenue 
curve. The EBIT loss this quarter reflects entirely our investment in product R&D. 
Excluding this investment, the core business is generating money at an EBIT level and is 
self-sustaining. These are deliberate choices that lay the foundation for a Company of

meaningful scale, and we will continue to make them in line with our strategy. In our 
custom ASIC, we closed large turnkey projects and have a very healthy pipeline in excess 
of $100 million. Our power product business or ASSP, which is central to our long-term 
strategy, we continue to invest in product development for the high voltage and low voltage. 
Our process wafers and probe test flows have been qualified and we are working with the 
leading ecosystem partners to lock specifications ahead of our first customer samples, 
which will happen towards the end of this year or early next year. 
 
Let me give you a brief outlook of what is happening in the semiconductor industry. The 
industry is in a strong demand cycle, driven by AI, but supply is tight. Foundries are 
running at full utilization and capacity is constrained across the ecosystem, which is leading 
to higher wafer prices and longer planning cycles. We expect this to continue to weigh on 
our margin in the immediate term. The shortage and rising cost of memory is also affecting 
end demand in consumer and edge AI applications, which are our focus areas. As a result, 
we expect some softening in the pace of growth in the coming quarters, though we are quite 
confident that the growth demand remains strong and that the markets will continue to 
support our strength. 
 
In DLM, we delivered another very strong quarter, supported by sustained order momentum 
and disciplined execution. The business has maintained positive orderbook momentum for 
six consecutive quarters, with book-to-bill ratio in excess of 1.6 times. The order book 
surpassed the record level achieved in the previous quarter and is highest it has ever been. 
Revenue grew more than 26% year-on-year in INR and we continue to meet customer 
requirements despite supply chain shortages, longer lead times and geopolitical uncertainty. 
DLM has significantly strengthened its sales leadership and continues to invest in strategic 
capabilities and operating foundation to support the next phase of growth. While these 
investments have a near-term impact on margin, they are important in building a scalable, 
sustainable, and stronger business. The focus firmly remains on profitable growth, operating 
leverage, and sustainable margin improvement over the medium to long term. Looking 
ahead, the structural drivers across DLM’s target markets continue to remain very 
favorable, including rising electronic content, growing AI infrastructure demand, global 
supply chain diversification, and broader outsourcing trends. With our differentiated design-
led manufacturing model, strong customer relationships, and expanding execution 
capabilities, Cyient DLM is very well positioned to capitalize on these opportunities and 
overall we delivered a very strong first half with revenue more than 30% over the first half 
of last year and we enter the second half of the year with a very strong order book, a robust 
pipeline, and a very strong and motivated sales force that will continue to deliver into the 
future. 
 
The Board also took cognizance of the cash generation and the strong operating 
performance, and we will continue this momentum into Q3 and into the rest of the year. Our

approach to capital allocation, as you know, remains balanced and disciplined. We will 
prioritize investments that drive long-term growth, keep financial flexibility to pursue 
strategic acquisitions where they make sense, and will continue to pay dividends in line 
with our policy. Consistent with this, I am pleased to share that the Board has declared an 
interim dividend of Rs.12 per share. We remain focused on sharp execution and on creating 
sustainable value for our shareholders and are very confident on our ability to generate cash 
as a group. At a group level, looking ahead, our focus is on opportunities that brings 
strengths to our business together. 
 
Defense, Semiconductors, and AI are the industries that present the highest growth 
opportunities, and I am very pleased and proud to say that Cyient is strongly positioned and 
is pursuing significant strategic opportunities in all these areas. We bring customers an end-
to-end proposition spanning engineering, silicon, manufacturing, lifestyle support, 
reinforcing the compounding value of our complementary capabilities. I want to reiterate 
that the three fastest growing sectors of Defense, Semiconductor and AI are where we, as a 
group, have significant capabilities that nobody else can match within our competitive set. 
With this, I hand over the call to Sukamal, who will take you through the business 
performance of Cyient. Sukamal over to you. 
Sukamal Banerjee: 
Thank you, Krishna. Good evening to all of you, and thank you for joining us today. At our 
Investor Day in August, we shared our perspective on the opportunities ahead for Cyient, 
the role we see for lifecycle engineering in shaping our future, and the priorities that will 
guide our next phase of growth. We also introduced our new brand promise, Nothing Less, 
giving a clearer voice to the exemplary outcomes that have shaped our work and our 
customer relationships. As we look at our Q2 performance, I am encouraged by strong 
progress we are making to drive predictability and profitability across the business. We 
delivered growth during the quarter, recorded our highest ever order intake for Q2, highest 
EBIT in 10 quarters, and remained focused on building the capabilities that support our 
long-term strategy. An important part of that capability expansion was welcoming the TAO 
Digital team to Cyient. Their expertise adds depth to what we can do for our customers, and 
our teams are already pursuing opportunities together. 
 
Let me now take you through our financial performance first across four metrics. Revenue 
for the quarter was US$174.2 million, which was up 7.5% quarter-over-quarter and 6.3% 
year-over-year in constant currency. This includes one month of revenues from the TAO 
Digital acquisition. On an organic basis, the revenue grew 1.6% quarter-over-quarter and 
0.4% year-over-year in constant currency. Our EBIT margin stood at 14.2%, up 107 basis 
points quarter-over-quarter and 206 basis points year-over-year. We recorded highest ever 
Q2 order intake of $158.4 million, up nearly 21% year-over-year, with positive momentum 
across both new businesses in existing and new customers from an order intake perspective. 
This does not consider any order intake from TAO consolidation, which we will start

they have signed up with us consists of a broad range of engineering services, which will be

to execute on the same on a go forward basis. I wanted to highlight this contract because of 
its significance but also wanted to share that we remain consistent on how we announce our 
order intake at Cyient versus how it may get captured by some of our peers. 
 
Technology order intake stood at $10.3 million, up 39.7% year-over-year, reflecting the 
demand we are seeing for the capabilities we are building in data, AI, digital engineering, 
and intelligent engineering solutions. The strength of our order intake, together with 
continued growth in our pipeline, gives us a greater confidence as we enter the second half 
of the year. Focusing on our market clusters and market units, transportation and mobility 
again grew strong at 4.5% quarter-over-quarter and 16.5% year-over-year in constant 
currency terms. It is the sixth consecutive quarter of growth for this particular segment. The 
shining light of this quarter and over previous couple of quarters has been our performance 
in automotive and mobility. Despite the challenges in the market, we continue to see robust 
growth in this market segment for Cyient. Growth is supported also by continued 
momentum in commercial aviation where our focus on aftermarket services and helping 
customers improve operating efficiency is delivering results, alongside a greater emphasis 
on systems and avionics. We see medium to long-term opportunities emerging in defense 
supported by sustained geopolitical demand or demand created by geopolitical actions 
while rail continues to demonstrate moderate recovery. Despite potential pressure from 
aviation fuel prices and inflation, our strategy, customer base capabilities, and the industry 
standing gives us confidence in sustaining this business performance. 
 
Networks and infrastructure was flattish with a slight degrowth of 0.3% quarter-over-
quarter in constant currency and a 1% year-over-year growth, largely reflecting completion 
of certain project-based engagements and some weakness in our utilities business. We 
continue to reshape the portfolio towards longer-term growth, more recurring programs, and 
we hope to make some announcements on these lines very soon. Even so, the underlying 
demand remains strong, continued fiber rollouts and the global build-out of AI data centers 
are sustaining well in demand, while rising power needs and grid modernization are driving 
investment in network design, asset data, and spatial intelligence. 
 
Strategic markets de-grew 1.5% on constant currency basis quarter-over-quarter. However, 
at the outset, let me state we are at the bottom of our business in some of these markets, 
especially energy, where we see growth ahead. In energy and process industries, the go-to-
market teams we rebuilt are starting to deliver. We have steadily pivoted the business

Switching over now talking about capability development and making sure that we continue 
to invest in the future, the opportunities we see across our business are closely linked to the 
capabilities we have been building. To support customers more effectively across the 
lifecycle, we are continuing to strengthen those capabilities. The integration of TAO Digital 
adds depth to our platform software and data engineering capabilities, and our teams are 
now taking this combined expertise to the customer engagements. This expands the support 
available to build stronger data foundation and enterprise AI adoption, complemented by 
our understanding of customer engineering environments, products, and operations. It 
further strengthens that we can offer in automotive, high tech, and health tech, and adds 
delivery capabilities in Greece and Taiwan. We are also bringing our engineering 
knowledge, data, and AI expertise together through newly established business unit, 
Intelligent Engineering Solutions to develop and commercialize repeatable and scalable 
solutions for our customers. CYiNGINE our agentic AI enabled lifecycle engineering 
intelligence platform, brings together governed industrial data, deep engineering domain 
knowledge, and modern AI stack to help customers improve outcomes across engineering, 
service, and quality. It enables three playbooks in engineering, three playbooks in terms of 
the value that we deliver to customers across engineering means faster design lifecycles and 
better first-time rates. In service, it means higher asset availability and fewer unplanned 
outages. In quality and regulatory world, it means faster certification with audit ready-
traceability. Each is measured against the customer’s own KPIs, which positions us well for 
long-term outcome-based engagements. Our progress in this area has received several 
recognition. One of them in Q2 was the Frost & Sullivan, who awarded Cyient with 2026 
Global Technology Innovation Leadership Recognition in the Intelligent Lifecycle 
Engineering Services space. 
 
Looking further ahead, we are evolving our technology organization through the creation of 
a CTO office with a focus on research and development in Horizon 2 and Horizon 3

quantum and other emerging technologies. This office will work across the group 
companies of DET, DLM and Semiconductors, identifying technologies with relevance 
across the group and building capabilities through collaboration with startups, academic

commercialization between the two groups that we have set up. So, talking now about

support customers across the products and the asset lifecycle. We already work across all 
nine stages, building on our engineering relationships to take on broader role through longer

discrete service activities to becoming a strategic partner across full asset lifecycle, helping 
customers improve reliability, performance, and operational efficiency. Our Agentic AI 
MRO offering launched this quarter in Q2 is a key enabler to that growth and is already 
generating strong customer interest. Supporting customers over these long operating 
lifecycles carries a responsibility to understand the outcomes they depend on. Our promise, 
Nothing Less, expresses that standard, we bring that responsibility, exemplary outcomes, 
and the resolve to reach beyond them, sustained through engineering discipline and an 
understanding of what each customer needs. The goals we set in Mumbai stand. I would

continued guidance for the results we have delivered. With that, let me invite Shrinivas

through FY2027 and to help offset the wage increases we are expecting in Q3 and Q4. We

on the external commercial borrowings raised for the TAO Digital acquisition. The

free cash flow was Rs.214 Crores or nearly 140% conversion of PAT that is up 87.9% 
sequentially and 36.3% year-on-year. The drivers were higher operating profit, three-day 
reduction in the net DSO and favorable working capital movements.
